title: Svitolina Opens Up on Her Toughest Year: "There Is No Completely Happy Life for Me"

 After a grueling season on and off the court, Svitolina has climbed back into the Top 10 and secured her spot at the WTA Finals. She opens up about her mindset heading into the tournament.
 Elina Svitolina during the fourth round of Wimbledon in 2024. © AFP Arthur Millot 08/11/2026, 10:14 3 min to read Follow us Indian Wells Svitolina WTA Finals Elina Svitolina is set to return to the WTA Finals, seven years after her last appearance.
 Crowned champion in 2018, the Ukrainian is back among the world's top eight players after a particularly grueling season, marked by several personal challenges.
 Remove ads At a press conference, she reflected on her journey and the changes that have helped her return to her best level.
 Back among the top eight after seven years
 "I'm very proud of the effort I put in to get back to this level after all these years and to reclaim my place among the top eight players.
 It's a fantastic feeling. I'm really happy to be here and to have the opportunity to play well."
 A break that transformed her season
 Svitolina also spoke about the importance of the break she chose to take at the end of last season to regain physical and mental freshness.
 "I give a lot of credit to that decision, because last year I was truly exhausted by everything that was going on.
 I'm someone who needs to take breaks and step back to recharge. It was important for me.
 Looking back, I'm very grateful that my team supported that decision.
 We sat down together to discuss this rest period, the training, and the preparation for this season, with the goal of giving my maximum.
 The season is very long, and you need to be fresh and ready to face the tough moments."
 A faster, more aggressive game
 "My game has changed a lot. The tour is now very different in terms of playing styles. Everything is much faster and tennis is more aggressive.
 If you don't seize your chances quickly, your opponents won't let you. That has also forced me to adapt and evolve my game.
 I'm still in that process, but I'm very happy with how my season has gone and to finally have the opportunity to return to the WTA Finals."
 Svitolina and her search for happiness
 "I've been through a difficult year, with a lot on my mind. Living in the public eye isn't easy either: everything is exposed and people can judge or comment on everything.
 I try to focus on the things I can control and to find moments of happiness every day.
 There probably isn't a completely happy life for me, given everything I have to deal with on a daily basis.
 But I can create happy moments with the people around me. That's something I can control."
 Stakhovsky, a new asset on her team
 Svitolina also discussed the arrival of Sergiy Stakhovsky on her team. The former Ukrainian player (world No. 31 in 2010) is helping her improve in an area that has never been her strength: net play.
 "He has taught me a lot about volleying and helped me improve in that area, which has never been one of my strengths.
 Now I can at least say that I'm capable of hitting a few good volleys from time to time. I'm really happy to be working with Sergiy.
 He's someone very close to me, we've known each other for a very long time, and that makes things easier. I'm happy to have him by my side to help me."
